entry.title: IIT Hyderabad Develops Metal-Free CO₂ Battery Technology for Future Space Missions | Made in India

media:group.media:title: IIT Hyderabad Develops Metal-Free CO₂ Battery Technology for Future Space Missions | Made in India
media:group.media:description:
Researchers at IIT Hyderabad (IITH) are developing an innovative, sustainable, metal-free CO₂ battery technology with potential applications in future space missions, including Mars exploration.
Designed to utilise carbon dioxide, this next-generation battery research aims to reduce dependence on expensive metals, improve sustainability, and explore lightweight energy storage solutions for space applications.
Using carbon-based electrodes and advanced electrochemical processes, the research team is working towards environmentally friendly battery technology that could also benefit Indian industries and support indigenous manufacturing.
Watch this special feature to discover how IIT Hyderabad is advancing homegrown innovation and exploring new possibilities in sustainable energy storage and space technology.

entry.title: Exploring Animation, Filmmaking, AI & Future of Creative Education II Prof. Nina Sabnani & Ms. Anne

media:group.media:title: Exploring Animation, Filmmaking, AI & Future of Creative Education II Prof. Nina Sabnani & Ms. Anne
media:group.media:description:
How has animation evolved from traditional filmmaking to the digital age? What responsibilities do filmmakers and content creators carry in an AI-driven world? And how can cinema connect people across cultures?
In this engaging episode of the IITH Podcast, **Prof. Ashok Kumar Pandey, Dean (Academics), IIT Hyderabad**, welcomes **Prof Nina and Ms. Anne** for an insightful conversation on the evolution of animation, filmmaking, visual storytelling, creative education, and the growing influence of Artificial Intelligence.
The discussion explores the remarkable journey of animation—from traditional 35mm filmmaking to today's digital technologies—and its expanding role in gaming, education, communication, and everyday life.
The guests also share their experiences in cinema and animation, including the influence of Indian films on cross-cultural connections, the transformation of creative education, and the importance of responsible storytelling.
A key highlight of the conversation is the impact of **Artificial Intelligence on creative industries**, particularly the challenges of distinguishing AI-generated content from reality and the responsibility of creators to maintain transparency, authenticity, and ethical practices.
The episode also touches upon the emerging opportunities in photography, filmmaking, and animation education, highlighting the importance of integrating creativity, technology, and interdisciplinary learning.
🎬 Key Topics Discussed: - Evolution of animation and filmmaking - Traditional filmmaking versus digital technologies - AI in creative industries and education - Ethics, authenticity, and responsible content creation - Indian cinema and cross-cultural storytelling - The future of photography, filmmaking, and animation education - Creative learning and interdisciplinary collaboration
🎧 Watch the conversation to discover how technology, creativity, and responsible storytelling are shaping the future of visual communication.

entry.title: तकनीक के सहारे भारत की सदियों पुरानी विरासत को बचाते युवा NextGen Bharat

media:group.media:title: तकनीक के सहारे भारत की सदियों पुरानी विरासत को बचाते युवा NextGen Bharat
media:group.media:description:
Proud to share that the Digital Heritage Lab (DHL) PI: Dr Shiva Ji, #IITHyderabad, has been featured by ANI and DD News, highlighting our efforts to harness advanced technologies for the documentation, preservation and interpretation of India's rich architectural and cultural heritage.
🔗 Watch the feature: https://youtu.be/7LqdRq2ODTQ
At the Digital Heritage Lab, we are exploring how LiDAR, photogrammetry, 3D documentation, GIS, AI, Digital Twins, and AR/VR/XR can bridge the gap between our civilizational past and technological future.
Our research brings together heritage architecture, material science, climate-risk assessment and immersive digital experiences. Through our DST-supported research, including the Digital Immersive Heritage Experience and risk assessment of historically significant temples in Kashi, we aim to make heritage documentation more scientific, conservation more informed, and cultural knowledge more accessible to future generations.
For us, digital heritage is not merely about creating 3D models of monuments. It is about understanding the stories, knowledge systems, craftsmanship and living traditions embedded within them—and using technology responsibly to safeguard this invaluable legacy.
Our vision: From documenting monuments to building living digital knowledge systems for India's heritage.

entry.title: Building the Future: IITH Students Design High-Speed PCB Innovations | Prof. B. S. Murty, Director

media:group.media:title: Building the Future: IITH Students Design High-Speed PCB Innovations | Prof. B. S. Murty, Director
media:group.media:description:
Building a culture of innovation through hands-on learning!
At IIT Hyderabad, students are encouraged to move beyond theory and create technologies that solve real-world challenges.
In this video, Prof. B. S. Murty, Director, IIT Hyderabad, shares the institute's vision of nurturing a strong maker culture where students design, build, and innovate from the ground up.
The video also features Prof. Y. Prem Kumar from the Department of Electrical Engineering, who introduces the PCB Design Course, where students gain practical experience by designing and fabricating printed circuit boards (PCBs) as early as their second year.
Featured Student Projects
* LCR Meter for laboratory applications * USB 2.0 High-Speed Hub (up to 320 Mbps) * High-Frequency Low Noise Amplifier (100–150 MHz) * High-speed PCB Design using Altium Designer * Signal Integrity, Impedance Matching & High-Frequency PCB Design
These projects demonstrate IIT Hyderabad's commitment to experiential learning, engineering excellence, and developing globally competitive technologies.

entry.title: Turning Every Flood Report into Actionable Data | SnapFlood – IIT Hyderabad

media:group.media:title: Turning Every Flood Report into Actionable Data | SnapFlood – IIT Hyderabad
media:group.media:description:
Floods can vary greatly from one location to another. SnapFlood, a citizen-powered innovation from IIT Hyderabad, transforms ground-level flood images and videos into valuable data for better understanding, planning and forecasting.
By bringing citizens into the process, SnapFlood is building a global flood database with real-time reported flooding instances as alerts that can support citizens, municipal agencies, disaster-management authorities, researchers, planners and communities in helping them to make more informed decisions and building more flood-resilient cities.

entry.title: IIT Hyderabad inaugurates 100-foot National Flag at Main Gate on Independence Day

media:group.media:title: IIT Hyderabad inaugurates 100-foot National Flag at Main Gate on Independence Day
media:group.media:description:
IIT Hyderabad marked the 80th Independence Day with a series of activities reflecting the spirit of nation-building, sustainability, innovation and service, with more than 10,000 native trees planted across the campus, taking the Institute's cumulative plantation on its present campus to the landmark milestone of one lakh saplings. The plantation drive, focused on ecological restoration using native Deccan species, represents IIT Hyderabad's sustained commitment to creating a campus that is not only greener but also more ecologically rich and better suited to the region's natural character.
The day's celebrations also began with the hoisting of the National Flag on a 100-foot-high mast pole at the Main Entrance of IIT Hyderabad, adding a new symbol of aspiration to the campus. The towering flag reflects the spirit of rising higher and contributing to nation-building, resonating with the motto of IITH, “Inventing and Innovating in Technology for Humanity”.
Watch the Video by @arshivaji capturing the glimpses.

entry.title: Beyond Earth: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla on His Journey to Space at IIT Hyderabad

media:group.media:title: Beyond Earth: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla on His Journey to Space at IIT Hyderabad
media:group.media:description:
What does it take to go from being an Indian Air Force fighter pilot to becoming an astronaut and representing India in human spaceflight?
In this special podcast conversation, Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, astronaut and member of the historic Axiom-4 mission, joins Prof. Ashok Kumar Pandey, Dean Academics, IIT Hyderabad, for an engaging conversation on his remarkable journey, space exploration, astronaut training, leadership, perseverance and the future of India’s space programme.
During his interaction with the IIT Hyderabad community, Group Captain Shukla shared insights from his journey—from the cockpit of the Indian Air Force to space—and discussed the challenges, experiences and lessons from astronaut training and life in a space mission.

entry.title: 15th Convocation | Chief Guest Address by Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam | IIT Hyderabad

media:group.media:title: 15th Convocation | Chief Guest Address by Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam | IIT Hyderabad
media:group.media:description:
Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam, Padma Vibhushan awardee, renowned Bharatanatyam exponent, scholar, and Distinguished Professor at IIT Hyderabad, delivered the Chief Guest Address at the 15th Convocation of the Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH).
In her thought-provoking address, Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam highlighted the timeless relationship between science, technology, arts, culture, and ancient Indian knowledge systems. She encouraged the graduating Class of 2026 to blend scientific excellence with creativity, ethics, and wisdom while contributing to society and nation-building.
Drawing from India's rich civilizational heritage, she reflected on the importance of interdisciplinary learning, the harmony of science and the arts, and the enduring values that shape innovation and human progress.
Highlights of the Address The synergy between science, technology, and the arts India's ancient knowledge systems and their relevance today The role of creativity, culture, and ethics in innovation Integrating modern scientific thought with timeless wisdom A message of purpose, humility, and lifelong learning for graduates
